_comment: What each platform accepts for a short vertical video's upload text, read off the platform's own pages on the date given. A value only third parties report says so in its source. Units matter: YouTube counts the description in UTF-8 bytes and tags with their separators; TikTok's API counts the caption in UTF-16 code units.

youtube.title_source: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57404 ("Video titles have a character limit of 100 characters"), read 2026-11-16
youtube.description_source: https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos (snippet.description: "maximum length of 5000 bytes"; the help page 57404 says 5,000 characters), read 2026-11-16
youtube.tags_source: https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos (snippet.tags[]: 500 characters for the list; commas count, and a tag with a space counts as if quoted), read 2026-11-16
youtube.hashtags_source: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6390658 (more than 60 hashtags: every hashtag is ignored; up to three appear by the title), read 2026-11-16
youtube.angle_brackets_source: https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos (title and description: every valid UTF-8 character except < and >), read 2026-11-16

tiktok.caption_source: https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/content-posting-api-reference-direct-post (post_info.title: "The maximum length is 2200 in UTF-16 runes"; the app itself is reported to accept 4,000), read 2026-11-16
tiktok.hashtags_source: reported, not published by TikTok: an in-app cap of "Maximum 5 hashtags" since Aug 2025 (https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/tiktok-implements-five-hashtag-limit-per-post/757857/), read 2026-11-16
tiktok.own_business_disclosure_source: https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/content-posting-api-reference-direct-post (brand_organic_toggle: "Set to true if this video is promoting the creator's own business"; brand_content_toggle is a paid partnership for a third party), read 2026-11-16
